content:
New article up on my website, about who really pays when a tribunal claim is brought. Spoiler: it's the employer. Win or lose.


Defending a simple claim to a final hearing can run to £4,500-£8,000 plus VAT. Discrimination and whistleblowing claims regularly go past £50,000. And you get none of it back if you win 🙄

Costs orders against a losing claimant are barely a thing. In 2023/24, just 153 went to employers, and the median was £3,000.

I'm all for an accessible tribunal (genuinely, before anyone gets their pitchfork out). People who've been badly treated need somewhere to go that doesn't require a war chest.

But that same design protects the speculative claim too.

And the backlog can't tell them apart.

So the employee with a real case waits behind it. Some hearings are being listed for 2029!

Then there's ChatGPT-drafted pleadings, early conciliation doubling to 12 weeks, and the time limit for claims going from three months to six. None of that makes the queue any shorter.

My advice to employers is to treat tribunal exposure as a business risk and price it before the ET1 arrives, not after.

Full article here: https://lnkd.in/gn9uzFDs

In the meantime, I'll be over here reading AI-drafted grievances and playing spot the prompt 🫠

content:
Sending documents over email has been giving me the ick for some time. It's just not secure.


But using Sharepoint gives me worse ick. I diligently change the settings for each share so that only the individual meant to receive the document can see it. Check again. And still, the person at the other end can't open it. 

In Practice Hub, I designed a system that means you can upload documents on your view and your client can download them at their end. Really secure, much better than sending via email. 

You can't share documents with employees using this method, though. And that's been bugging me. There was a tipping point a couple of months ago when an employee got super nasty with me because they couldn't download a recording of a hearing I'd sent them. 

I decided to take ACTION to stop difficult file sharing once and for all! 

So I built Secure Share. It's really simple, employees sign in using their email and a magic code, download, upload. My favourite bit is that you can see exactly when they logged in and hit the download button (no more "but I didn't get the letter"!). 

You can also set access to a period of time of your choosing, and revoke access at any time. 

Have a watch of this funky video (loving the music). 

Rocket the cat insisted that I put some orange cats in it and said he'd bring me a spider while I slept if I didn't. 

We’ve made a fully functional demo account already filled with example clients, cases and documents. No card, no sales call. Just have a look around. Have a look here and you’ll be emailed a link: https://lnkd.in/g2-_Khw2

content:
Rocket Digital has left the building. Practice Hub HR Ltd has moved in.


Turns out naming your company after your product saves a lot of explaining. We live and learn. 

Rocket Digital Ltd has become Practice Hub HR Ltd. 

This is because I'm no longer doing websites for HR consultants, so the rename made sense. This company will now be 100% laser focussed on making Practice Hub absolutely awesome! 

In case you don't know what I'm on about, Practice Hub is a platform for HR consultants built by an HR consultant! 

It has the usual CRM-ish stuff, but also client and case management, socials hub, e-signing, client portal, employee documents, employee contract signing, to do list, billing, invoicing (or connection to your software), transcription, calendar bookings, emails, automated attendance notes... the list is growing. 

Everything is unlimited, except for transcriptions but you get a generous allowance and can buy a top up if needed. 

When I say unlimited, I mean: 
🚀Social media posts. As many feeds and posts as you can think of! 
🚀Document signing. None of this "five envelopes per month" business. 
🚀Calendar bookings. If you're anything like me, you'll have at least 15 email addresses to manage for clients. Hook them all up to ensure no one double books. No limits there. 

There's too many features for me to put in a post right now, but the main purpose of it is that all the systems that an HR consultant could ever need are in one home. 

Simple for your admin, and for your bottom line! 

You can learn more and access your own demo account here: https://lnkd.in/gX_8QsQj

First 14 days free!

content:
Happy Information Commission day! 


Today is the day that the Information Commissioner's Office becomes the Information Commission.

It's such a big deal that even the IC haven't bothered to update their website with the new name. 

Your policies and contracts will likely still refer to the ICO, unless you are using one of my updated versions from The HR Vault  🎉 

But the DUAA basically says don't worry about it. Leave it under the old name forever if you want. We do not care! 

You can read all about it in the Vault's updated legal update here: https://lnkd.in/g_hK9XzW
